title: Signs of zero and NaN through FLOAT and DOUBLE operations
verdict: IEEE in arithmetic; one zero in comparisons, hashing and sort keys; FLOAT `least`/`greatest` canonicalise
description: Arithmetic is IEEE on both widths, so it keeps and makes `-0.0`. `+`, `-`, `*` and `/` on FLOAT and DOUBLE are the C++ operators on `float` and `double` (no promotion of `float`), unary `-` is `-x` (it flips the sign of `0.0` and of a NaN), and `%` is `std::fmod`, whose zero takes the dividend's sign (`-4.0 % 2.0 = -0.0`). The optimizer's arithmetic simplification rewrites only integer `x + 0`, `x * 1`, …, and for doubles only `x / 1`, which keeps the sign; so it does not change a zero's sign.

Comparisons see one zero. `=`, `<`, `>` and `>=` on floats are C++ `==`, `<`, `>` after the NaN cases, so `-0.0 = 0.0` is true and neither is below the other. Hashing (GROUP BY, joins, DISTINCT) maps `-0.0` to `+0.0` and every NaN to the quiet NaN, and the sort key encodes both zeros alike, so ORDER BY treats them as peers, and the next key or the input order decides. ORDER BY carries FLOAT and DOUBLE columns in the payload, since the key loses the sign.

`least` and `greatest` on DOUBLE keep the first argument among equals (`least(-0.0, 0.0)` is `-0.0`, `least(0.0, -0.0)` is `0.0`). On FLOAT there is no direct instantiation: they compare sort keys and decode the winner from its key, so a zero comes out as `+0.0` and a NaN as the positive quiet NaN. Builds with `DUCKDB_SMALLER_BINARY` route DOUBLE the same way.

A NaN's sign survives arithmetic, negation and the FLOAT-to-DOUBLE cast (a plain conversion), and `signbit` has a FLOAT overload that reads it (`std::signbit`). Hashing and the FLOAT `least`/`greatest` drop it.
DuckDB's own test notes that a checkpoint loses the sign of zero in storage (DuckDB issue 25580), unrelated to ORDER BY.
reference: `zero_sign: ONE_ZERO` and `nan_kind: ONE_NAN` (#89, docs/core-semantics.md); Substrait is IEEE. sverify's SQL canonicalises `-0.0` on every read and after each operation that can make it (`Dialect.canon`, duckdb-R14), so DuckDB's IEEE zeros never reach a result. Lean refuses FLOAT arithmetic (duckdb-R12).

evidence.note: only x / 1 is simplified for FLOAT/DOUBLE; +, -, * only for integral results
EqualsFloat, GreaterThanFloat, GreaterThanEqualsFloat, ComparatorFloat: NaN cases, then C++ comparisons
FloatingPointEqualityTransform: -0.0 to 0.0, NaN to quiet_NaN, before hashing
EncodeFloat/EncodeDouble: x == 0 gives one key; every NaN the top key; DecodeFloat/DecodeDouble give +0.0 and quiet_NaN
the sort key is not injective around zero, so FLOAT/DOUBLE columns go through the payload
SortKeyLeastGreatest: decodes the result from its sort key
a later argument replaces the result only when strictly less (greater)
direct instantiations for integers, DOUBLE and VARCHAR; FLOAT falls back to sort keys
signbit: FLOAT and DOUBLE overloads, std::signbit
require noforcestorage: checkpointing loses the sign of zero (issue 25580); ORDER BY keeps signbit

provenance.notes: The float and double specialisations are written out per type, so the reading covers fp32 and fp64 separately.
